chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When you intend to enter the state of Ihram at a time other than that of an obligatory prayer, pray two rak'ahs, then enter Ihram after them."

key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.غَيْرِ وَقْتِ: At a time other than / not during the time of

ai.seo_question: How should one enter Ihram if not during the time of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the procedural flexibility for entering Ihram outside the standard prayer times by prescribing two voluntary rak'ahs as a preparatory act, ensuring ritual purity and spiritual focus. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on integrating voluntary acts of worship to bridge gaps in obligatory timings, thereby maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrimage state. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of fiqh in accommodating the pilgrim's immediate intention while adhering to established ritual protocols.
